WEEK 6 LAB · SELECTION AND JOINS
:::

# Connect players to the games they save

The video game platform needs useful lists of players and their saved games. Use the relationships in the database to produce those lists, then check that each result connects the right records.

:::

## Questions and submission

[Download the Word questions and response template](lab-02-sql-joins-response-template.docx){download="lab-02-sql-joins-response-template.docx" .btn .btn-primary}

The Word document contains all five questions and spaces for your SQL, output, and explanations.

- Work individually or in a group of two or three; **each student submits their own completed portion of the Word document in Canvas**.
- **This is a participation grade. Submit as much as you complete; you do not need to finish every question by the end of class.**
- Include your name and collaborators. See Canvas for the due date.

## Set up the video game data

Use `video_game`, `player_account`, and `save_file` from the previous lectures. **Reset these practice tables and load the supplied data** so everyone uses the same IDs and rows.

[Download the lab setup SQL](lab-02-video-game-setup.sql){download="lab-02-video-game-setup.sql" .btn .btn-primary}

- Connect to your personal schema. Run the file by copying its SQL into `psql` or using `\i /path/to/lab-02-video-game-setup.sql`.
- The file drops any existing versions of these three tables, recreates them, and inserts three games, three players, and eight saves. Recreating the tables restarts their generated IDs.
- It first drops `save_file` and the earlier practice tables `play_session` and `player_game_library`, if present, because they reference games or players. The reset replaces their existing practice data; it does not touch the escape-room assignment tables.
- If you already ran this setup for the joins lecture and have not changed the data, continue with those tables. Otherwise, rerun the file to reset them. Keep the supplied data unchanged while completing the lab.

### Saved games

Each row represents one saved game belonging to one player. A player can have multiple saves for the same game.

| save_id | player_id | game_id | saved_at | completion_percent | slot_label |
|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | 1 | 1 | 2026-09-24 09:00-06 | 25.00 | `NULL` |
| 2 | 1 | 1 | 2026-09-24 10:00-06 | 50.00 | `NULL` |
| 3 | 2 | 1 | 2026-09-24 09:00-06 | 49.99 | favorite |
| 4 | 1 | 1 | 2026-09-24 11:00-06 | 75.00 | `NULL` |
| 5 | 3 | 2 | 2026-09-24 09:00-06 | 80.00 | `NULL` |
| 6 | 3 | 2 | 2026-09-24 10:00-06 | 100.00 | favorite |
| 7 | 2 | 3 | 2026-09-24 10:00-06 | `NULL` | new run |
| 8 | 2 | 3 | 2026-09-24 11:00-06 | 80.00 | `NULL` |

Completion is a percentage: `80.00` means 80%, and `NULL` means progress has not been reported. A `NULL` slot label means the save is unnamed. Timestamps include a UTC offset of −06; your client may display the same instants in another time zone.
